bio: In the heart of Seville, on a pedestrian back street behind City Hall, this elegant bistro bears the same name as the street where it stands, a small tribute to the guild of children's shoe makers that once existed here (in times gone by, these shoes were called ‘chicarros’). Inside, with its sophisticated eclecticism, you will be offered a contemporary European-style menu with constant nods to Spanish produce. One of the most popular dishes is the matured beef steak tartare with marrow from the shank bone....
